summary: Lakshman Joo was a scholar in philosophy, Indology, and religious studies who studied under Maheshwar Nath Razdan (1926–1933). He founded the Universal Shaiva Fellowship in 1991 and taught numerous students, including Lilian Silburn, André Padoux, and Alexis Sanderson.

Lakshmi Swaminathan worked in Indology and linguistics. She studied at Queen Mary's College (~1930–1932) and Madras Medical College (~1932–1938), later serving as a retired lecturer at Stony Brook University.

Lal Mani Joshi worked in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Indology, earning his PhD under Govind Chandra Pande at Gorakhpur University. He taught at Gorakhpur and Punjabi University, with visiting posts at Harvard, Amherst, Haverford, and CIHTS.
Lalchandra Bhagawandas Gandhi was an Indology scholar. He served as a Jain Pandit at the Central Library of Baroda and held a post at the Maharaja Sayajirao University of Baroda, attested in 1939.

Lama Jabb is a Tibetologist who served as a Junior Research Fellow at the University of Oxford. He is also attested in 2026 as the Head of the Tibetan & Himalayan Studies Centre at Wolfson College, Oxford.

Lama Jampa Thaye is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who earned a PhD at the University of Manchester and studied under traditional teachers including Karma Thinley Rinpoche. He serves on the international teaching faculty at Karmapa International Buddhist Institute.

Lama Kunga Rinpoche is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied at Ngor Monastery and served there as Thartse Shabthung in 1959. In 1973, he founded the Ewam Choden Tibetan Buddhist Center.

Lama Thubten Zopa Rinpoche was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology figure who studied under Yeshe Thubten, Geshe Rabten, and the 14th Dalai Lama. He founded Kopan Monastery, FPMT, Maitripa College, and served as FPMT's spiritual director from 1984.
Lama Tsering Gyaltsen is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University and with the traditional teacher Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje.
Lama Yeshe Gyamtso works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under the traditional teachers Kalu Rinpoche (attested 1996) and Lama Norlha.

Lambert Schmithausen is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He studied under Erich Frauwallner and Paul Hacker, later serving as associate professor at the University of Münster (1970–1973) and on the Advisory Board at the University of Hamburg (1973–2005).

Lance E. Nelson specializes in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy, earning his doctorate at McMaster University by 1986. Attested as a professor at the University of San Diego in 1997, he also taught James Blumenthal.

Lance S. Cousins worked in Buddhist studies and Indology, studying at Cambridge under Harold Walter Bailey and K. R. Norman. He taught at Manchester (~1970–2000) and Oxford (~2000–2015), and served as President of the Pali Text Society (2002–2003).

Lang Chen specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. Chen completed a PhD at Yale University, studying with doctoral supervisors Koichi Shinohara and Phyllis Granoff as well as teacher Janet Gyatso.

Lang Eun Ra is a scholar in philosophy and Buddhist studies who completed doctoral studies at Temple University under supervisor Charles Wei-hsun Fu, also studying with Bibhuti S. Yadav, Norbert Samuelson, and Leonard Swidler.

Lara Braitstein specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, earning a PhD at McGill University under Richard P. Hayes. She holds a post at McGill University as Associate Professor of Indo-Tibetan Buddhism, attested in 2026.
Laren Hogen Bays specializes in Buddhist studies and religious studies and studied under traditional teacher Shodo Harada. Bays founded Great Vow Zen Monastery and serves as its co-abbot.

Larry DeVries is an Indology and religious studies scholar who earned a PhD at the University of Minnesota. He taught at Minnesota, Hawaiʻi, and Washington, held a research post at Chicago, and was affiliated with Langara College in 2005.

Lars Fogelin specializes in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Indology, completing a PhD at the University of Michigan (1995–2003) under Carla M. Sinopoli. He has held academic posts at Albion College, Southern Illinois University, and the University of Arizona.

Lars Martin Fosse works in Indology, linguistics, and computational studies. He studied at the University of Oslo (~1971–1997), Heidelberg University, and the University of Bonn, and is attested as a teacher at Oslo in 2002.
